newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam coffee comes out, but moisture woes linger.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee comes out, but moisture woes linger.

text.p: Vietnam's new robusta crop from Dak Lak province is beginning to reach the market as heavy rains which made drying and transport difficult appears to have lifted, coffee traders said on Wednesday.
"Coffee is beginning to move from Dak Lak. It's pretty much in full flow," a senior coffee dealer for a Western commodity house said.
But another dealer from a U.S. trading company said moisture levels in the beans remain uncomfortably high at around 15-17 percent against the desired level of about 13 percent.
"The moisture level is still a problem. The weather in Dak Lak is now okay, but it's not over yet," he said, adding there were still lingering worries over rain returning to the area.
Dak Lak province, located in the highlands of Vietnam, produces two-thirds of the 240,000-270,000 tonnes of coffee beans exported by Vietnam each year.
Estimates of the amount of coffee beans sold and shipped by Vietnam in the past week ranged between 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes against only a few hundred tonnes in the preceding week, traders said.
"Significant quantities are being sold and shipped now. There's been a very active business in beans," one dealer said.
Exports for November are expected to reach around 20,000 tonnes. "That's not bad considering they had a very slow start," a trader said.
Trading in Indonesian robusta coffee remains thin since most of the crop has already been sold and the new crop will not come into the market until the following March.
"Indonesia is not going to be a hotbed of activity for the next few weeks," a trader said.

Prices of Vietnam's Grade 2, 80 percent black and broken, robusta beans were quoted in a range between US$1,080-$1,150 a tonne FOB Saigon port, against last week's $1,090-$1,140 a tonne, traders said.
Indonesian Grade 4 robusta beans were seen at about $1,250 a tonne FOB Panjang port, slightly higher compared to the $1,200-$1,250 a tonne last week, dealers said.
LIFFE robusta coffee futures are expected to inch up about $5-$10 in steady but quiet dealings this afternoon, traders said.
"It might be slightly higher, but I don't think it will be active. With New York down two days ago and ending mixed last night, I don't see a big move this afternoon," a coffee dealer said.
"London is caught in a very narrow range. The trend there will be affected by New York," another trader said, adding the most active January contract should remain locked between $1,400 to $1,500.
The January contract finished $18 higher on Tuesday at $1,448, marginally off the day's high of $1,449.
Singapore March robusta coffee futures closed at $1,273 a tonne on Tuesday after four tonnes were traded at $1,230.
The market was closed for a holiday on Monday. A total of seven tonnes were traded on Friday.
Three tonnes of the January contract settled at $1,336 a tonne and four tonnes of the March contract finished at $1,296 a tonne on the Singapore Commodity Exchange on Tuesday.
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
